title: Public Relations Explained Simply | Marketing Management Ep 31
description:
Laddoo Lab has ads, offers and ten shops, but few people know the story behind it. Then a local reporter visits Nani's kitchen, and the next morning Nani is in the newspaper. Zoya did not pay for that story. She earned it. In this animated lesson we use Laddoo Lab, a millet laddoo brand from Bengaluru, to understand public relations (PR).

You will see Philip Kotler and Gary Armstrong's definition of public relations, a brand's publics (customers, neighbours, the press, shopkeepers and the government), and a step-by-step run of how the Nani story happened: find a true story, write a press release, invite the press, the story runs, and share it everywhere. We meet more PR tools (events, community work and social media) and see news, events, community work and handling bad news at work today in a hospital, a bank, a bakery and an airline. We also look at the human side honestly: a news story earns more trust than an ad, but you can't control what reporters write and bad news spreads fast. When a parent posts that a pack was stale, Zoya replies the same day, and we hear how Ivy Lee's statement after a 1906 train crash in America is often called the first press release.

This is Episode 31 of our Marketing Management series for MBA, BBA and commerce students.
